title: Eight step records admit a chosen id that names nothing the record holds
instrument: a per-record refine plus a parts.test case each; AND an experiment over a COPY of part_records (temp GRAVITONE_STORE_PATH) counting stored rows that would become unreadable - only 0 there makes the tighten safe
evidence: probe: SCORE.schema.safeParse({v:1,spots:[{id:'s',title:'',sceneIds:[],takeIds:[],activeTakeId:'t'}]}).success === true; ADS_SCORE {takeIds:[],activeTakeId:'t'} true; STILL {takes:[],adopted:'x'} true. Only VOICE refines (packages/domain/src/steps/parts.ts:238-240). Unrefined: still.ts adopted, finish.ts:40 spot.activeTakeId, finish.ts:61 ads-score activeTakeId, research.ts:233 ads-ideas pickedId, script.ts:322 ads-scenarios pickedId, frames.ts:105 frames-alts activeId, frames.ts:122/124 ads-shots adoptedImage/adoptedClip
body:
## Summary
Of the nine step-record fields that pick one of the record's own items, only VOICE's refuses a dangling id; the other eight admit an id that names nothing.

## Description
packages/domain/src/steps/parts.ts:238 VOICE refines that a line's active take is among its takes, citing 'v1's score held the same rule per spot' - but SCORE (finish.ts:40), ADS_SCORE (finish.ts:61), STILL (still.ts adopted), ADS_IDEAS/ADS_SCENARIOS pickedId, FRAMES_ALTS activeId and ADS_SHOTS adoptedImage/adoptedClip do not. v1 held the score rule in the WRITER (lib/score/takes.ts:103), not the door. Fixed = each door refuses a dangling pick, as VOICE does. Risk: a stored row with a dangling pick becomes unreadable (decodeStep refuses the whole record as malformed), so the tighten needs a store-copy count first.

## Flow
- SCORE.schema.safeParse(spot with activeTakeId 't', takeIds []) -> success
- a reader resolves the active take -> undefined -> the cut/render finds no take
- fix: a refine per record, then count existing rows that would fail on a store copy

## Expected impact
An editor or producer that resolves a pick no longer meets an id with nothing behind it; what could break is reading a stored record that already dangles.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every pick names a held item
Before: 1 of 9 pick fields refined; 3 dangling probes admitted
After: (B) 9 of 9, with 0 stored rows made unreadable on a store copy
Method: probe - schema probes on 3 records; the store-copy count is the experiment this round did not run (it needs the operator's store copied)
Result: better
Gate: none
drain_note: operator-only: needs a copy of the operator store to count rows that would become unreadable

title: Pausing a part reads the whole project as blocked, not waiting
evidence: probe: partStatesOf([cut, gate:cut<-cut, slot<-gate:cut], {cut: paused}, true) -> cut paused, gate:cut blocked, slot blocked; projectStateOf -> 'blocked'. packages/domain/src/plan.ts:28 STUCK includes paused; plan.ts:125-129 'a paused part counts as waiting (queued)'
body:
## Summary
projectStateOf promises a paused part reads as waiting, but partStatesOf marks everything after a paused part blocked, so any plan with a successor reads blocked.

## Description
plan.ts:125-129 says the prototype's fall-through to `draft` was fixed so a paused part counts as waiting (queued). But plan.ts:28 puts `paused` in STUCK, so every part after it is `blocked` (plan.ts:53-55, the prototype's blockedBy), and projectStateOf's `has("failed","blocked")` fires first: the paused-as-queued branch is reached only when the paused part has no successor, which no recipe has (every work part has a gate after it). Fixed = one of: a paused upstream makes successors `queued` (waiting), or the project reads `queued` when its only blocks trace to a pause. The Projects list groups `blocked` as needing the operator, so an operator's own pause lands in that group. Which word a pause shows is the operator's call.

## Flow
- pause the cut part of a launched trailer
- gate:cut and slot read blocked
- projectStateOf -> blocked; the shelf files it under blocked

## Expected impact
An operator who pauses a project stops seeing it filed as needing attention; a reader that treats blocked as an incident stops counting pauses.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a paused project reads waiting, as the docstring states
Before: 3-part plan with the work part paused -> project blocked
After: (either fix) -> queued
Method: probe - the derivation run on the plan shape every recipe has
Result: better
Gate: direction
